correctness.rationale: The global negative-cubic side is established by a finite-horizon first-crossing barrier: \(x\) and \(y\) grow at most linearly with a prior curvature bound, so coupling is \(O(R^2)\) while the restoring cubic is \(O(R^3)\). On the positive cubic side a uniform high-curvature invariant bootstrap yields two open finite-time escape sectors; changing to curvature as the independent variable proves finite x,y limits, the square-root pole, the \(\alpha/(3\gamma)\) constant, and integrated velocity/position tails. At zero cubic gain a logarithmic-velocity bootstrap proves finite blow-down, a simple curvature pole, and the \(-1/(2\alpha)\) correction. The standalone checker verifies the local inverse-series coefficients and finite diagnostics but is not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: Forward completeness is a basic qualitative property needed to interpret global chaotic-flow simulations. The source varies cubic feedback through zero, yet the two signs have radically different maximal-existence behavior: globally complete for negative cubic feedback versus open finite escape for zero or positive. The transition also changes the curvature blow-up exponent from one to one half and converts divergent logarithmic velocity into finite limiting velocity; the exact second coefficients are canonical diagnostic predictions, not arbitrary parameter slices.
